text:
Notes for future self (matmul, n≈1000):

- Attempt 0 reached 10.3 ms (206x over naive) with three pieces: B packed into 16-wide column panels, a 6x16 register-blocked microkernel using GCC vector extensions (v4 floats via memcpy loads), and pthreads with an atomic work queue over 48-row chunks. K blocking at KC=256 keeps A rows and the panel slice in L1/L2. With -march=native the compiler likely widens the v4 ops into AVX/FMA, but I haven't checked the generated assembly.
- I made only one attempt, so I have no ablations. I can't say how much each piece contributed.
- Weaknesses:
  - A is not packed, so the kernel uses strided scalar loads from 6 rows.
  - The loop order runs over every panel for each chunk, which leaves the B panel slice (KC×NR) small but gives poor reuse of A across panels.
  - Threads are created twice per call. That spawn overhead is noticeable at 10 ms.
- Next steps:
  - Pack A into MR-interleaved blocks.
  - Use 8-wide vectors (v8 / AVX2) with an 8x8 or 6x16 kernel and explicit FMA. Check whether the machine is ARM (NEON, where the darwin host suggests possibly Apple M-series) or x86.
  - Tune MC/KC/NC for L2/L3 in the BLIS-style ordering.
  - Merge packing and compute into one parallel region, or use an OpenMP persistent pool.
  - Try -O3 -march=native -ffast-math -funroll-loops.
